Deploying a static site on Amazon S3

A complete walkthrough for hosting staticsite.bandarkarami.com — from bucket creation to a CloudFront-fronted, SSL-secured domain on Route 53.

Regionap-south-1 (Mumbai)
Domainbandarkarami.com
StackS3 · CloudFront · ACM · Route 53
Amazon S3
Store static website files
CloudFront
CDN for global content delivery
Route 53
Domain and DNS management
ACM
SSL/TLS certificate management
IAM
Access control and permissions
01
Request path
Architecture diagram
  • Internet users request the site by domain name.
  • Route 53 (DNS) resolves the domain to the CloudFront distribution.
  • CloudFront serves the cached response over SSL/TLS, pulling from the origin on a cache miss.
  • S3 static website acts as the origin, holding every asset.
  • The bucket stores the raw HTML, CSS, and other site files.
02
IAM
Permissions required
Amazon S3 Full Access
CloudFront Full Access
Route 53 Full Access
ACM Full Access
03
Walkthrough
Implementation
1
Create the bucket
AWS Console → S3 → Create Bucket
  • Bucket namestaticsite.bandarkarami.com
  • Regionap-south-1 (Mumbai)
S3 → Buckets — staticsite.bandarkarami.com created in ap-south-1
2
Upload site files
Upload the site's contents into the bucket root
📄 index.html
📁 css/
📁 images/
Bucket contents after upload
3
Enable static website hosting
S3 Bucket → Properties → Static website hosting
  • Static website hostingEnable
  • Index documentindex.html
Properties → Static website hosting → Enable
4
Configure the bucket policy
Permissions → Block public access → turn off
Block public access — set to Off
Public read access is required for visitors to load pages directly from the bucket. Scope the policy to GetObject only — never grant write or delete to the public.

Attach the following statement under Permissions → Bucket policy:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "PublicReadAccess",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:GetObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::staticsite.bandarkarami.com/*"
    }
  ]
}
Permissions → Bucket policy — applied
5
Create the SSL certificate
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
  1. Open ACM and request a certificate
    Navigate to Certificate Manager → Certificates and click Request.
  2. Choose a public certificate
    Select Request a public certificate, then Next.
  3. Provide the domain name
    Enter the fully qualified domain name and keep the remaining settings at their defaults, then click Request.
  4. Certificate issued
    Once DNS validation completes, the certificate status reads Issued.
6
Create the CloudFront distribution
CloudFront → Distributions → Create distribution
  1. Select plan and get started
    Choose the Free plan.
    • Distribution namestaticsite.bandarkarami.com
    • Distribution typeSingle website or app
    • Domainstaticsite.bandarkarami.com
  2. Specify origin
    Set Origin type to Amazon S3, then point the S3 origin field at the bucket: staticsite.bandarkarami.com.s3.<region>...
  3. Enable security
    Leave the included WAF protections at their defaults and click Next.
  4. Get a TLS certificate
    Attach the certificate issued by ACM in the previous step.
  5. Review and create
    Confirm every setting, then click Create distribution.
7
Configure Route 53
Route 53 → Hosted zones → bandarkarami.com

Create the DNS records that point the subdomain at the CloudFront distribution:

  • Record typeA — alias to CloudFront
  • Record typeAAAA — alias to CloudFront
  • Record typeCNAME
04
Verification
Test the website
Live endpoint
https://staticsite.bandarkarami.com
Served via CloudFront · SSL/TLS active
